name: Federal Republic of Nigeria

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Land area 910,770 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2, mid); high is surface area incl. inland water 923,768 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 237,527,782). Low allows for census uncertainty; high adds one year of growth to 2026 (~2.5%/yr).

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2024 p.509 as quoted: 143,000 active (Army ~100,000, Navy ~25,000, Air Force ~18,000 in earlier editions). CIA Factbook 2025 ~140,000 (low). High is World Bank MS.MIL.TOTL.P1 223,000 (2020), which adds the 80,000 paramilitary.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2024 as quoted lists no organised reserve (0). High is an allowance for recallable ex-servicemen (educated judgement). Paramilitary (80,000, NSCDC etc.) excluded.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 143,000 (IISS 2024) minus infantry P roles (25,000 + 55,000) = 63,000: Navy ~25,000, Air Force ~18,000, armour/artillery crews, logistics, staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Regional analogy: very large youthful population but no conscription, no reserve system and no stocks to equip mass levies; scaled well below 20th-century total-war ratios (8-15%). Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Infantry of the mechanised and armoured brigades (1 Mech, 3 Armd, 81 Div elements); Army ~100,000 (IISS as quoted on the personnel list). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigerian_Army)

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: mixed BMP/Saurer/MRAP fleet, poor maintenance (Nigerian Army article: "exceptionally poor standard of maintenance").

training.note: Rubric 0.5: volunteer regulars with long COIN experience (Boko Haram/ISWAP since 2009) but weak combined-arms training.

count.note: Educated guess. Motorised/light infantry and COIN brigades (Operation Hadin Kai deployed up to ~70,000 troops in the northeast at times, CIA Factbook 2025). (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/africa/ni.json)

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: small arms, Hilux technicals, some MRAPs.

training.note: Rubric 0.5: combat-experienced in COIN, uneven training.

count.note: MBT list (IISS-derived): T-55 24 + T-72 16 + Vickers Mk3 108 + AMX-30 16 = 164 (mid). High is the Army equipment list total (VT-4 17 + T-72 ~41 + T-55 ~100 + Vickers ~172 = 330), which includes unserviceable hulls.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25: Vickers Mk3/T-55 a generation behind; 17 VT-4 are modern.

training.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: low readiness of armoured units.

count.note: Army equipment list: BMP-1/2 62 + ZSD-85 60 + Saurer 4K 250 + MT-LB 67 + Piranha I 110 + BTR-3U 47 + BTR-60/70 24 + Phantom II 24 + Streit MRAPs 237 + CS/VP3 310 + Ezugwu 80 + PF ARA 40 + Reva 40 + Cobra 204 ~ 1,555 (high). Mid discounts ~15% for unserviceable legacy vehicles. Recce cars (~514 Scorpion/AML/ERC/VBL/Cascavel) excluded.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: mostly wheeled MRAP/APC, few IFVs.

count.note: Army list: SH-5/SH-2 15 + Palmaria 25 + APR-40 25 + BM-21 5 + RM-70 7 + D-30 90 + D-74 90 + M46 7 + D-20 4 + FH77 24 (in storage) + OTO Mod 56 124 = 416 (high). Mid drops stored FH77 and assumes ~80% of the rest serviceable.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: towed Cold War guns, very few MLRS.

count.note: Air Force list: JF-17 Block II 3 + F-7Ni 5 = 8 (FT-7Ni trainer excluded; one F-7 lost Oct 2025).

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: JF-17 is a light 4th-generation fighter, F-7 obsolete.

training.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: very small fighter force.

count.note: A-29 Super Tucano 12 + Alpha Jet 13 (8 of the original 24 active plus 12 newly delivered, 6 operational) = 25. Low counts 12 + ~6 serviceable Alpha Jets. 24 M-346FA on order.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: COIN aircraft with PGMs, no survivable strike jets.

count.note: Air Force 62 (AW109 18, H125 2, Bell 412 2, AS332 5, EC135 3, Mi-171 6, Mi-35 15, T129 6, AW139 3, AW189 2) + Navy 19 (Lynx 3, AW109 14, AW139 2; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigerian_Navy) + Army UH-1 2 = 83. Attack: Mi-35 15 + T129 6; 12 AH-1Z on order.

Group 2+ only: Air Force Wing Loong II 5 + CH-3A 3 + CH-4B 3 + Yabhon Flash-20 2 = 13; Army TB2 6 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Nigerian_Army); Navy Aerostar 9 + AR-500B 4 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigerian_Navy) = 32. 12 Aksungur on order.
Nigerian Navy fleet table: Thunder-class (ex-USCG Hamilton cutters, F90/F93) 2 counted as frigates; MEKO 360 Aradu (F89) refitting (high).

quality.note: Rubric 0.25: ex-coastguard cutters with guns only, no AAW/ASW.

count.note: Centenary (P18N) OPV 2 + 31 active patrol vessels + Lerici MCM 2 + LST-100 1 = 36. Inshore craft (Manta, RHIBs, gunboats ~90) excluded; missile boats inactive.

Battery conversion (SOURCES.md): Roland 16 launchers ~4, ZSU-23-4 30 ~7, ZU-23-2 350 towed guns at ~6 per battery ~58, Bofors L/60 12 ~2 = 71 (high). Mid assumes ~2/3 serviceable. MANPADS (Blowpipe 48, Strela 100) excluded.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25 minus: mostly 23 mm guns; Roland obsolete; no modern SAM.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: functioning joint staff and long operational experience (MNJTF, ECOMOG history), but corruption and inter-service coordination problems limit effectiveness.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: national volunteer army; desertion and morale problems reported in the northeast campaign.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: long attritional COIN war; higher for defence of the homeland.

weapons.note: Between anchors 8 (1943) and 9 (1985): mostly Cold War small arms and artillery; some PGMs (Chinese guided bombs, Cirit) and UCAVs.

armor.note: Anchor 8-9: Vickers Mk3/T-55 (1960s), few VT-4; MRAP-heavy fleet.

ships.note: Anchor 8-9: ex-USCG cutters and Chinese OPVs, no missile-armed combatants in service.

fortification.note: Anchor 8: field fortifications and super-camps in the northeast; no layered air defence.

logistics.note: Anchor 8-9: motor transport, 3 C-130H; weak sustainment.

communications.note: Anchor 9: satellite comms (NigComSat), limited data links.

isr.note: Anchor 9 minus: King Air/DA62 ISR, MALE UCAVs; no military satellites beyond NigeriaSat imaging.

air.note: Anchor 8-9: JF-17 Block II and A-29; no air-superiority fleet.

cyber.note: Anchor 9 minus: Defence Space/cyber commands nascent.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 0.91% of GDP in 2025. Low/high +/-15-20%; security spending outside the defence budget (police, NSCDC) excluded.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction (and mining/oil where present) 16.4% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). +/-2 points.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Net food importer (rice, wheat) with large subsistence agriculture; most surplus feeds the cities. Not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 120,177,737 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share aged 15-19 11.387% / 5 = 2,737,040. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10%.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Defence Industries Corporation and Proforce assemble Ezugwu, ARA and Viper MRAPs/light armour (80+ Ezugwu delivered). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Nigerian_Army)

roadKm.note: Road list (2017): 195,000 km total (high), ~60,000 km paved (mid). Low is World Bank IS.ROD.TOTL.KM 57,626 km (2005).

railKm.note: asOf 2015: 3,528 route-km (World Bank IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). CIA Factbook 3,798 km (2014) spans the range. Only a few lines operational; the standard-gauge Lagos-Ibadan and Abuja-Kaduna lines are new.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 28 ports, 2 large + 1 medium = 3 (Lagos/Apapa, Port Harcourt/Onne); high adds Calabar, Warri, Lekki deep-sea port (2023).

merchantTonnage.note: Nigerian-flag fleet 7,156 thousand DWT (4,467 thousand GT). Low allows for registry ships not trading for Nigeria.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Truck-borne sustainment along few paved roads; COIN brigades operate from super-camps.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Donkeys, camels and horses in the north (not from FAO data); militarily marginal.

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1: familiar terrain and local supply; large population support; no fortified depth.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data, 2026 order of battle. Equipment counts from Wikipedia equipment lists (Army, Air Force, Navy; many Army entries from deliveries, not IISS active figures) cross-checked with the IISS-derived main battle tank list; serviceability is poor and counts are grade C. Population convention: everything inside ne:NGA (World Bank). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. ships_major = frigates (incl. ex-Hamilton cutters); drones = Group 2+ only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Internal wars: Boko Haram/ISWAP (northeast), banditry (northwest), Niger Delta militancy. Paramilitary (NSCDC, police mobile force) excluded. Global Firepower used only as a cross-check.
